Cluster significant peptides into contiguous destabilized/protected regions

Source: R/residue_regions.R
residue_regions.Rd

Takes a peptide-level comparison between two states at one timepoint and derives contiguous residue regions that are consistently destabilized (more exposed) or protected (less exposed), rather than reporting a flat list of significant peptides. A peptide counts as significant by the same rule as everywhere else in the package: Welch p-value below pvalue (raw, or adjusted with p_adjust) AND absolute difference above the pooled Hageman & Weis critical interval. A residue enters a region only once at least min_peptides distinct significant peptides of the same direction cover it, so a single peptide alone cannot create a region. Charge states of the same peptide count once.

Usage

residue_regions(
  df,
  state1,
  state2,
  times,
  replicates = 3,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  p_adjust = "none",
  min_peptides = 2,
  gap_tolerance = 2,
  alpha = 0.01,
  fdr_cutoff
)

Arguments

df

output of output_tp() called with percent = FALSE, i.e. deuteration uptake in Daltons - this function works in Da so that delta is additive across residues, same requirement as residue_deconvolution().

state1

First protein state, matched the same way as in plot_fissure_vent().

state2

Second protein state, same matching rule.

times

a single Deut.Time value to derive regions for (e.g. "1800.00s"). Call this function once per timepoint of interest and rbind() the results if you want regions across multiple timepoints.

replicates

number of replicates in sample, only used for tables without named replicate columns. Default set to 3.

pvalue

p-value cutoff for a peptide to count as significant. Default 0.01.

p_adjust

multiple-testing correction of the per-peptide Welch p-values, passed to stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default) or e.g. "BH", applied across the peptides of the comparison.

min_peptides

minimum number of distinct, same-direction, significant peptides that must cover a residue before that residue is included in a region. Default 2.

gap_tolerance

maximum number of consecutive non-covered residues allowed inside one region before it is split into two. Default 2.

alpha

alpha of the pooled Hageman & Weis critical interval (CI_2pts()), the same threshold plot_fissure_vent() draws as its grey band. Default 0.01.

fdr_cutoff

deprecated. Earlier versions called a peptide significant when its BH-adjusted p-value was below fdr_cutoff, without the critical-interval condition. Supplying it reproduces that rule, with a warning.

Value

data.frame with one row per region: direction ("destabilized"/"protected"), region_start, region_end, n_residues, n_peptides (distinct significant, same-direction peptides overlapping the region), mean_per_residue_delta (Da per exchangeable amide), and pooled_CI_Da (the pooled critical interval for this comparison, repeated on every row for reference).

Details

The per-residue effect reported for a region is each covering peptide's difference divided by its number of exchangeable amides (nb_exch_deut()), averaged over the peptides covering each residue.

See also

plot_fissure_vent(), residue_deconvolution(), residue_level_average()

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm, percent = FALSE)
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written
residue_regions(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
#>   direction region_start region_end n_residues n_peptides
#> 1 protected           62         63          2          2
#> 2 protected           95        124         30          6
#>   mean_per_residue_delta pooled_CI_Da
#> 1            -0.07548611    0.2392609
#> 2            -0.04715929    0.2392609
